title: Degree bound for a zero slice
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb{N}$ and let $f:\mathbb{F}_2^{n+1}\to\mathbb{F}_2$ have algebraic degree at most $k$. If the slice obtained by fixing the first coordinate to $1$ is identically zero, then the slice obtained by fixing it to $0$ has algebraic degree at most $k-1$, where subtraction is truncated in $\mathbb{N}$.
hypotheses_covered: The slice at first coordinate $1$ is identically zero
The algebraic degree of $f$ is at most $k$
